newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices mixed on poor supply, demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices mixed on poor supply, demand.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Thursday were mixed with Punjab cotton seeing gains while Gujarat varieties suffered losses, dealers said.
Punjab extended gains amid dwindling supplies at the tail end of the season as well as a shortage of ready stock. Daily arrivals in the Punjab region dropped to 400/500 bales (170 kg each).
In spot deals Punjab saw-ginned rose to 1,775/1,900 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) from 1,720/1,825 rupees. Bengal-deshi gained by 5/10 rupees at 970/1,010 rupees per maund.

Gujarat cotton lost recent gains amid demand resistance by millers at higher levels which prompted light profit-taking. Gujarat Kalyan slid by 200 rupees at 14,500/14,800 rupees per candy (355.56 kg). Wagad cotton however remained steady at 13,200 rupees per candy and kala-ginned at 12,700 rupees.
